title: Hello, terminal
story: You've been hired to write the start-up message for a small pizza shop's ordering terminal. When the program starts, it announces itself, says how many slices the night's dough makes, and shows the opening time in a neat format.

requirements.text: The first line printed is exactly `Python is running`.
It prints the number of slices from 24 pizzas with 8 slices each. Python must do the multiplication.
It prints the time as exactly `18:30`, using `print` with two values and `sep`.
It has at least one comment.

steps: Print how many slices 24 pizzas of 8 slices make. Write the multiplication, not the answer.
Print `18:30` by giving `print` the two values `18` and `30` and choosing a separator.
Add a comment explaining one of your lines.
hints: Text goes in quotes. The multiplication doesn't, so Python works it out.
`sep=":"` goes after the values, inside the same brackets.

static.fail: Let Python do the multiplication: write `24 * 8` in your code.
Use `print`'s `sep=` setting to put the colon between the two numbers.
Add a comment: a line (or the end of one) starting with `#`.

cases.fail: None of the lines had the number of slices.
